clue.text: Blue-green coat is mine — river's damaged outside

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters go round the synonym for mine
damaged letters are knocked out of shape, so the word river's is rearranged

parts.note: to mine is to dig

explanation.surface: A painter reports that some blue-green finish has been spoilt on the outside by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' reads as a possessive but is the verb dig; 'damaged' makes VERRIS from the river's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdigris is the green-blue film of corrosion that forms over copper and brass, literally a coating.

clue.text: See gold cross on entrance for former pleasure garden

parts.note: V abbreviates vide, Latin for see
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
an X is a cross
a hall is an entrance hall

explanation.surface: A visitor notes a golden cross over the gateway to an old garden.
explanation.walkthrough: VAUXHALL Gardens was a famous London pleasure garden of the 18th and 19th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Vauxhall Gardens in south London was a celebrated Georgian venue for outdoor entertainment, now gone.

clue.text: Shape character of Greek doctor

parts.note: rho is a letter of the Greek alphabet
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A Greek physician's personality is being sized up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like personality but means a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhomb, or rhombus, is a four-sided figure with equal sides, a geometrical shape.

clue.text: Ruined home time slicing potatoes

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: slicing means the time letter cuts into the potato word

parts.note: taters is slang for potatoes

explanation.surface: Someone at home ruins the dinner, taking too long to cut up the spuds.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in tatters is torn to shreds, figuratively ruined, as with hopes or reputations.

clue.text: Test substance of date shown in lease

indicators.note: shown in puts the date word inside the lease word

parts.note: to rent is to lease
an age is a period or date in history

explanation.surface: A chemical's expiry date appears on a rental agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a chemical used to detect or test for another substance in a reaction.

clue.text: Promoter of scent containing even pieces of anise

indicators.note: containing means the scent word holds the picked letters

parts.note: spoor is the track or scent of an animal

indicators.note: even pieces are the second and fourth letters of the word anise

explanation.surface: Someone backs a perfume flavoured with aniseed.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponsor backs and promotes an event or person, usually with money.

clue.text: Grey and unfashionable plaster

parts.note: something out is no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: A dull, dated wall coating is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Grout is a thin mortar used to fill the gaps between tiles, a kind of plaster.

clue.text: Old cricketer's grand career

parts.note: G is slang for a grand, a thousand
to career is to race along at speed

explanation.surface: A retired cricketer had a wonderful time in the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning rush. W. G. GRACE was a famous Victorian English cricketer; cricket is England's summer bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: W. G. Grace was the great Victorian cricketer, long dead, so an old cricketer.

clue.text: Like birds round celebrity endlessly excite

parts.note: O is round in shape
a VIP, very important person, is a celebrity

indicators.note: endlessly drops the last letter of the synonym

parts.note: to arouse is to excite

explanation.surface: Birds circle a famous person, who gets them endlessly worked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Oviparous animals lay eggs that hatch outside the body, as birds do.

clue.text: Fragile £10 with no date for new note?

indicators.note: date for new means the date letter replaces the new letter

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note

explanation.surface: A delicate ten-pound note is reissued undated.
explanation.walkthrough: TENNER is the £10 note, the question mark hinting at that; 'date for new' swaps its N for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender meat or skin is soft and easily damaged, delicate and fragile.

clue.text: Submarine's left for a means of securing something

indicators.note: one letter for another means swapping it in, here the letter for left taking the place of a

parts.note: a U-boat is a German submarine

explanation.surface: A sailor explains that a submarine was abandoned to secure something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' looks like a verb (abandoned) but is L, which replaces the A of UBOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A U-bolt is a U-shaped bolt with threaded ends, used to clamp and fasten things.

clue.text: Trouble to dish out praise

parts.note: ado is fuss or trouble
to ration is to dole out or dish out in portions

explanation.surface: Handing out compliments, someone finds, is more bother than it is worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish out' tempts as an anagram signal, but it is the synonym RATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is worship, the highest kind of praise, as in the adoration of the Magi.

clue.text: Regular shade used outside a little

indicators.note: used outside tells us the colour word sits round the other piece

parts.note: a hue is a shade of colour
a bit means a little

explanation.surface: Someone always wears a particular colour on the outside, just a touch of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitue is a regular visitor to a place, such as a frequenter of a bar.

clue.text: Leak linking visit to young boy up in court

parts.note: to see someone is to visit them
a page is a boy attending a royal court

explanation.surface: A leak connects a visit with a child appearing before the magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up in court' suggests a lad in trouble with the law, but it is a royal court, where a page served.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly escaping through small gaps, a slow leak.

clue.text: Learning about criminal in test gets a boy to see sense

indicators.note: about means the learning word goes around the rearranged letters

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong or bent, so the letters of in test are rearranged

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy who has studied a criminal under examination comes round to common sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' turns the letters of 'in test' into ISTENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To listen to reason is the idiom for accepting sensible advice, which is to see sense.

clue.text: What obsessive does for peanuts and vegetables

definitions.meaning: an obsessive splits hairs, so one fussing over legumes would divide them in half
dried peas halved for soups and dhal

explanation.definitionFit: Split peas are dried peas divided in two, a vegetable staple of soups.

clue.text: Think highly of including unknown trade union in amalgamation

indicators.note: including means the admiring word holds the other pieces

parts.note: to admire is to think highly of
X is the classic unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Someone praises bringing an unnamed union into a merger.
explanation.definitionFit: An admixture is a mixture, something blended in, so a combination or amalgamation.

clue.text: Where dishwasher went cruelly wrong after last of rinses

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the picked letter
last of takes the final letter of rinses
wrong means the letters of cruelly have gone awry and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dishwasher broke down badly at the end of a rinse cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The dishwasher was a person, a scullery maid, not a machine.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery was the back kitchen where a servant washed the dishes.

clue.text: Form, one composed and universal — exactly so

definitions.text: Form, one composed and universal — exactly so

parts.note: a form is a school class
I is the Roman numeral for one
calm means composed
U is the film certificate for universal
sic, Latin for thus, marks a quotation given exactly so

explanation.surface: The clue describes a genre: something written by a composer and with appeal for all.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: music that is composed and universal.
explanation.definitionFit: Classical music is the art form of written-down compositions with lasting, universal appeal.

clue.text: Orwell's town Wigan is primarily swamped by bad chips

indicators.note: swamped by means the first letters are buried inside the rearranged chips
bad means the letters of chips have gone off and are rearranged
primarily takes the first letter of Wigan and of is

explanation.surface: George Orwell's town of Wigan is overwhelmed by poor chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orwell' suggests the author of The Road to Wigan Pier, but it is the River Orwell, on which IPSWICH, a Suffolk town, stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Ipswich, the county town of Suffolk, lies on the estuary of the River Orwell.

clue.text: Maiden taken in by a dreadful Romeo — this one?

definitions.text: Maiden taken in by a dreadful Romeo — this one?

indicators.note: taken in by means the maiden letter goes inside

parts.note: dire means dreadful
M is the cricket abbreviation for maiden
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A young woman is fooled by an awful Romeo, and the clue asks whether he is her suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a Romeo who woos a maiden is an admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is a suitor who courts a woman, just what a Romeo is.

clue.text: Step three beginning calculation in programming language

parts.note: a pas is a step in ballet

indicators.note: three beginning takes the first three letters of calculation

explanation.surface: Instructions for a three-step start to a calculation in code.
explanation.definitionFit: Pascal is a structured programming language devised by Niklaus Wirth around 1970.

clue.text: Mediterranean resort opposed to beds, with 500 being axed

parts.note: anti means against or opposed to

indicators.note: being axed means cut out, and what goes is D, the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A seaside town takes against hotel beds, with five hundred of them scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibes is a resort town on the French Riviera, on the Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Plant fibre packed round large slate

indicators.note: packed round means the fibre word goes around the size letter

parts.note: bast is fibre from the inner bark of plants

explanation.surface: Plant fibre is wrapped around a big roofing tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slate' looks like the roofing stone but is the verb meaning criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast and to slate both mean to criticise someone fiercely.

clue.text: Scottish scientist is the biggest possible bore

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the biggest possible
a bore is a hole drilled for water or oil, a well

explanation.surface: A Scottish researcher is mocked as the most tedious person around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bore' reads as a tedious person but is a drilled shaft.
explanation.definitionFit: James Clerk Maxwell was the Edinburgh-born physicist who formulated the equations of electromagnetism.

clue.text: Trouble following space communication

indicators.note: following puts the trouble word after the space word

parts.note: an em is a printing space
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A problem comes after a message from outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space' suggests the cosmos but is a typesetting em.
explanation.definitionFit: An email is an electronic message, a form of communication.

clue.text: Optimism about mostly sound old knight

indicators.note: about puts the optimism word around the other piece

parts.note: cheer is hopefulness or good spirits

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: a sound argument is a valid one

explanation.surface: A hopeful mood surrounds a fairly healthy elderly knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Chevalier is the French title for a knight or horseman, used of old cavaliers.

clue.text: Employment of learned person after university

indicators.note: after puts the learned person behind the university letter

parts.note: a sage is a wise or learned person

explanation.surface: A scholar finds a job once they have left university.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the use or handling of something, its employment for a purpose.

clue.text: Record includes unknown composer

indicators.note: includes means the record word holds the unknown letter inside it

parts.note: a list is a written record
Z is one of the letters used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A recording features a composer nobody has heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Antics succeeded in transforming hero Macbeth?

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for succeeded inside the rearranged letters
transforming changes the shape of the word hero, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: S abbreviates succeeded in genealogies
Macbeth is a play by Shakespeare, so it is an example of the word

explanation.surface: Someone managed to turn a heroic Macbeth into slapstick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transforming' makes HORE from the hero letters; the question mark flags Macbeth as an example, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Horseplay is rough, boisterous fooling about, which is the same thing as antics.
